types.name: date
types.doc: A date or partial date (e.g. just year or year + month). There is no time zone. The format is a union of the schema types gYear, gYearMonth and date. Dates SHALL be valid dates.

types.name: dateTime
types.doc: A date, date-time or partial date (e.g. just year or year + month). If hours and minutes are specified, a time zone SHALL be populated. The format is a union of the schema types gYear, gYearMonth, date and dateTime. Seconds must be provided due to schema type constraints but may be zero-filled and may be ignored. Dates SHALL be valid dates.

types.name: code
types.doc: A string which has at least one character and no leading or trailing whitespace and where there is no whitespace other than single spaces in the contents

types.name: string
types.doc: A sequence of Unicode characters

types.name: integer
types.doc: A whole number

types.name: oid
types.doc: An OID represented as a URI

types.name: canonical
types.doc: A URI that is a reference to a canonical URL on a FHIR resource

types.name: uri
types.doc: String of characters used to identify a name or a resource

types.name: uuid
types.doc: A UUID, represented as a URI

types.name: url
types.doc: A URI that is a literal reference

types.name: instant
types.doc: An instant in time - known at least to the second

types.name: boolean
types.doc: Value of "true" or "false"

types.name: base64Binary
types.doc: A stream of bytes

types.name: unsignedInt
types.doc: An integer with a value that is not negative (e.g. >= 0)

types.name: markdown
types.doc: A string that may contain Github Flavored Markdown syntax for optional processing by a mark down presentation engine

types.name: time
types.doc: A time during the day, with no date specified

types.name: id
types.doc: Any combination of letters, numerals, "-" and ".", with a length limit of 64 characters. (This might be an integer, an unprefixed OID, UUID or any other identifier pattern that meets these constraints.) Ids are case-insensitive.

types.name: positiveInt
types.doc: An integer with a value that is positive (e.g. >0)

types.name: decimal
types.doc: A rational number with implicit precision

types.name: Extension
types.doc: Optional Extension Element - found in all resources.

types.name: BackboneElement
types.doc: Base definition for all elements that are defined inside a resource - but not those in a data type.

types.name: Narrative
types.doc: A human-readable summary of the resource conveying the essential clinical and business information for the resource.

types.name: NarrativeStatus
types.doc: The status of a resource narrative.

types.name: Element
types.doc: Base definition for all elements in a resource.

types.name: Meta
types.doc: The metadata about a resource. This is content in the resource that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

types.name: Address
types.doc: An address expressed using postal conventions (as opposed to GPS or other location definition formats). This data type may be used to convey addresses for use in delivering mail as well as for visiting locations which might not be valid for mail delivery. There are a variety of postal address formats defined around the world.

types.name: AddressUse
types.doc: The use of an address.

types.name: AddressType
types.doc: The type of an address (physical / postal).

types.name: Contributor
types.doc: A contributor to the content of a knowledge asset, including authors, editors, reviewers, and endorsers.

types.name: ContributorType
types.doc: The type of contributor.

types.name: Attachment
types.doc: For referring to data content defined in other formats.

types.name: Count
types.doc: A measured amount (or an amount that can potentially be measured). Note that measured amounts include amounts that are not precisely quantified, including amounts involving arbitrary units and floating currencies.

types.name: DataRequirement
types.doc: Describes a required data item for evaluation in terms of the type of data, and optional code or date-based filters of the data.

types.name: DataRequirement.CodeFilter
types.doc: Describes a required data item for evaluation in terms of the type of data, and optional code or date-based filters of the data.

types.name: DataRequirement.DateFilter
types.doc: Describes a required data item for evaluation in terms of the type of data, and optional code or date-based filters of the data.

types.name: DataRequirement.Sort
types.doc: Describes a required data item for evaluation in terms of the type of data, and optional code or date-based filters of the data.

types.name: SortDirection
types.doc: The possible sort directions, ascending or descending.

types.name: Dosage
types.doc: Indicates how the medication is/was taken or should be taken by the patient.

types.name: Dosage.DoseAndRate
types.doc: Indicates how the medication is/was taken or should be taken by the patient.

types.name: Money
types.doc: An amount of economic utility in some recognized currency.

types.name: HumanName
types.doc: A human's name with the ability to identify parts and usage.

types.name: NameUse
types.doc: The use of a human name.

types.name: ContactPoint
types.doc: Details for all kinds of technology mediated contact points for a person or organization, including telephone, email, etc.

types.name: ContactPointSystem
types.doc: Telecommunications form for contact point.

types.name: ContactPointUse
types.doc: Use of contact point.

types.name: MarketingStatus
types.doc: The marketing status describes the date when a medicinal product is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.

types.name: Identifier
types.doc: An identifier - identifies some entity uniquely and unambiguously. Typically this is used for business identifiers.

types.name: IdentifierUse
types.doc: Identifies the purpose for this identifier, if known .

types.name: SubstanceAmount
types.doc: Chemical substances are a single substance type whose primary defining element is the molecular structure. Chemical substances shall be defined on the basis of their complete covalent molecular structure; the presence of a salt (counter-ion) and/or solvates (water, alcohols) is also captured. Purity, grade, physical form or particle size are not taken into account in the definition of a chemical substance or in the assignment of a Substance ID.

types.name: SubstanceAmount.ReferenceRange
types.doc: Chemical substances are a single substance type whose primary defining element is the molecular structure. Chemical substances shall be defined on the basis of their complete covalent molecular structure; the presence of a salt (counter-ion) and/or solvates (water, alcohols) is also captured. Purity, grade, physical form or particle size are not taken into account in the definition of a chemical substance or in the assignment of a Substance ID.

types.name: Coding
types.doc: A reference to a code defined by a terminology system.

types.name: SampledData
types.doc: A series of measurements taken by a device, with upper and lower limits. There may be more than one dimension in the data.

types.name: Population
types.doc: A populatioof people with some set of grouping criteria.

types.name: Ratio
types.doc: A relationship of two Quantity values - expressed as a numerator and a denominator.

types.name: Distance
types.doc: A length - a value with a unit that is a physical distance.

types.name: Age
types.doc: A duration of time during which an organism (or a process) has existed.

types.name: Reference
types.doc: A reference from one resource to another.

types.name: TriggerDefinition
types.doc: A description of a triggering event. Triggering events can be named events, data events, or periodic, as determined by the type element.

types.name: TriggerType
types.doc: The type of trigger.

types.name: Quantity
types.doc: A measured amount (or an amount that can potentially be measured). Note that measured amounts include amounts that are not precisely quantified, including amounts involving arbitrary units and floating currencies.

types.name: QuantityComparator
types.doc: How the Quantity should be understood and represented.

types.name: Period
types.doc: A time period defined by a start and end date and optionally time.

types.name: Duration
types.doc: A length of time.

types.name: Range
types.doc: A set of ordered Quantities defined by a low and high limit.

types.name: RelatedArtifact
types.doc: Related artifacts such as additional documentation, justification, or bibliographic references.

types.name: RelatedArtifactType
types.doc: The type of relationship to the related artifact.

types.name: Annotation
types.doc: A text note which also contains information about who made the statement and when.

types.name: ProductShelfLife
types.doc: The shelf-life and storage information for a medicinal product item or container can be described using this class.

types.name: ContactDetail
types.doc: Specifies contact information for a person or organization.

types.name: UsageContext
types.doc: Specifies clinical/business/etc. metadata that can be used to retrieve, index and/or categorize an artifact. This metadata can either be specific to the applicable population (e.g., age category, DRG) or the specific context of care (e.g., venue, care setting, provider of care).

types.name: Expression
types.doc: A expression that is evaluated in a specified context and returns a value. The context of use of the expression must specify the context in which the expression is evaluated, and how the result of the expression is used.

types.name: ExpressionLanguage
types.doc: The media type of the expression language.

types.name: Signature
types.doc: A signature along with supporting context. The signature may be a digital signature that is cryptographic in nature, or some other signature acceptable to the domain. This other signature may be as simple as a graphical image representing a hand-written signature, or a signature ceremony Different signature approaches have different utilities.

types.name: Timing
types.doc: Specifies an event that may occur multiple times. Timing schedules are used to record when things are planned, expected or requested to occur. The most common usage is in dosage instructions for medications. They are also used when planning care of various kinds, and may be used for reporting the schedule to which past regular activities were carried out.

types.name: Timing.Repeat
types.doc: Specifies an event that may occur multiple times. Timing schedules are used to record when things are planned, expected or requested to occur. The most common usage is in dosage instructions for medications. They are also used when planning care of various kinds, and may be used for reporting the schedule to which past regular activities were carried out.

types.name: UnitsOfTime
types.doc: A unit of time (units from UCUM).

types.name: EventTiming
types.doc: Real world event relating to the schedule.

types.name: ProdCharacteristic
types.doc: The marketing status describes the date when a medicinal product is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.

types.name: CodeableConcept
types.doc: A concept that may be defined by a formal reference to a terminology or ontology or may be provided by text.

types.name: ParameterDefinition
types.doc: The parameters to the module. This collection specifies both the input and output parameters. Input parameters are provided by the caller as part of the $evaluate operation. Output parameters are included in the GuidanceResponse.

types.name: ElementDefinition
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Constraint
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Mapping
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Base
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Type
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Example
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Slicing
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Binding
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: ElementDefinition.Discriminator
types.doc: Captures constraints on each element within the resource, profile, or extension.

types.name: PropertyRepresentation
types.doc: How a property is represented when serialized.

types.name: ConstraintSeverity
types.doc: SHALL applications comply with this constraint?

types.name: AggregationMode
types.doc: How resource references can be aggregated.

types.name: ReferenceVersionRules
types.doc: Whether a reference needs to be version specific or version independent, or whether either can be used.

types.name: SlicingRules
types.doc: How slices are interpreted when evaluating an instance.

types.name: BindingStrength
types.doc: Indication of the degree of conformance expectations associated with a binding.

types.name: DiscriminatorType
types.doc: How an element value is interpreted when discrimination is evaluated.

types.name: DomainResource
types.doc: A resource that includes narrative, extensions, and contained resources.

types.name: Resource
types.doc: This is the base resource type for everything.
